findings_not_failures.finding: GRID decode does quadratic work on a hostile .fig before any count bound. grid_tracks checks each gridRows/gridColumns entry for a repeated id with a linear scan of the tracks kept so far (nodes.rs:1361), and grid_sizes finds each sizing entry's track with a linear search (nodes.rs:1409). Kiwi arrays are bounded only by Limits (max_array_len and max_tree_values 16M, input 128 MiB), and the 1000-track bound (GRID_COUNT_MAX) is applied later, in the mapping. One frame with about 10^6 track entries costs about 5 x 10^11 comparisons inside one node, where document_from_tree checks the cancel token only between nodes. The lane note 'track lists come from the bounded kiwi value tree' overstates this. Same class as F-R43-3 and F-R44-7 (work done before the budget).

findings_not_failures.finding: The window's frame-rect walk can take exponential time, and the budget check comes after it. Geo::bounds of a group calls Geo::background, which calls bounds(child, 0) on every later sibling, resetting the depth that the 64-level guard counts (auto_layout.rs:204, :215). When the background test fails, bounds walks the same children again at depth + 1. A chain of d nested groups, each with a small first vector that does not contain the next group, costs about 2^d walks, and each walk scans every layer (children() is a linear filter). al_commit computes the container's own rect through locals() -> geo.rect before the MAX_SUBTREE (4096) and depth-32 checks of the loop apply (auto_layout.rs:284). It is reachable from any auto-layout command on such a frame (an imported .fig). Selecting the frame or drawing the section does not compute geometry.
findings_not_failures.repair_direction: pass depth + 1 (not 0) from background, memoise bounds per layer for one command, and charge the walk against MAX_SUBTREE before computing it
